newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen extending slide on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen extending slide on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover and analysts saw them falling again on Monday on the back of strong selling after price fixing, but said they should moderately rebound or at least slow falls later next week.
The main market's WIG index fell 1.8 percent, to 13,499.4, and turnover fell 6.4 percent to 92.9 million zlotys ($33.2 million) on both markets as 11 issues rose, 55 fell and 14 were flat.
Analysts said some demand was likely to appear, after the market already has fallen 10.5 percent since recording a high of 15,078.7 points of the WIG index on October 9.

"I think the market might extend its fall on Monday, but it should start looking a bit better later as it should react to the falls...Everyone is surprised it hasn't happened yet," said Dariusz Szepieniec, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

Some analysts said Thursday's surprise decision by the lower house of parliament to cut taxes for low-earners was unlikely to affect the market as the top rates were unchanged, but said the political turmoil could harm the bourse.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell two percent in a 24-million zloty turnover ($8.6 million) in regular session and fell 5.3 percent in 30.5-million-zloty (10.9 million) continuous trade.

Analysts said construction firm Espebepe extended its 18.3-percent plunge, falling 9.6 percent, after it said on Tuesday it could go bankrupt if it failed to clinch a debt restructuring deal with its creditors.
But they were surprised with Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE) 9.4-percent and Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) nine-percent falls.
